speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months; can you tell me if the pain is worse in the morning or after activity, and if you have noticed any redness or warmth over the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the fact that the pain is severe enough to wake you from sleep is concerning. Given your age and the lack of relief with ibuprofen, is the swelling localized specifically to the knee joint or does it extend into the surrounding tissues? Also, have you noticed any locking or clicking sensations in the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (likely Rheumatoid Arthritis or Seronegative Spondyloarthropathy) given the chronic duration, nocturnal pain, swelling, and age, though osteochondritis dissecans remains a differential. I will order an inflammatory panel and knee X-ray to confirm.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP, HLA_B27.
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_XRay_left_ap_lateral.
